text:
maria: Quick follow-up after the RBAC spike: proposed option A = pushdown row-filtering in the query planner (synthesize WHERE clauses based on principal/roles). Option B = proxy-layer mask + redact-at-read. Pros/cons?

sam: +1 to pushdown for performance (less data moved) but worried about policy surface. We have to ensure the planner emits predicates that are provably equivalent to projection-level checks. Hard for complex policies with resource-attribute predicates.

rachel: proxy masking is simpler policywise (single place to enforce), easier to audit, but blows up bandwidth and increases downstream CPU for masking. Also UX needs to know when something was redacted vs legitimately absent.

oliver: sketch of pushdown approach: at parse-time attach auth predicate like: `WHERE owner_id = :principal OR org_id IN (:teams)` then rely on existing index on (owner_id, org_id). For multi-join dashboards we can apply predicates to each table via join pushdown rules.

maria: example policy that breaks naive pushdown: "users can see records for projects where they have any of read/triage roles OR fields marked public". That translates to a predicate mixing ACL membership and per-row flag. We need IAM joins for membership, which may be expensive if evaluated per-query.

sam: possible hybrid: push down simple, deterministic predicates (owner, public flag), fallback to proxy for ACL-heavy results. Mark route as "best-effort" and surface telemetry: how often fallback triggered.

rachel: operational requirements: tokenized policy versioning. If we push predicates into planner, we must bind them to an auth_version so we can invalidate cached plans and prepared statements when policies change.

infra-bot: perf-estimate: pushdown reduces egress bytes by ~70% on synthetic dashboard workload. CPU on DB increases 10% due to extra predicate evaluation.

oliver: caching note: with pushdown we can safely cache prepared plans per (route, auth_version) and reuse them. Proxy masking can't reuse row slices as effectively because mask depends on principal.

maria: security check: any pushdown that uses cached auth predicates must expire quickly on role change events. We need an invalidation pipeline from IAM -> query-planner cache. Could be fanout to planner nodes with versioned keys.

sam: another risk: predicate-based pushdown leaks schema surface. e.g., if predicate uses `is_demo` flag internal to db, a user could infer presence of that flag via timing differences. Mitigation: plan to always hide predicate field names behind opaque functions or to normalize query timing. That seems hard.

rachel: UX/telemetry: dashboards should show "filtered for your access" indicator when pushdown applied and "some data redacted" when proxy masking occurs. Also record event: {route, tenant, method:pushdown|proxy, fallback}.

maria: rollout plan proposal: 1) implement policy compiler that emits pushdown predicates and auth_version, 2) run in read-only sim mode for 2 weeks (planner attaches predicates but still returns unfiltered results to compare), 3) enable pushdown for 5% of tenants (statistically selected), 4) monitor mismatch-rate (sample re-check with full projection auth), latency P99, and dashboard egress.

oliver: testing: add deterministic property tests that for a bunch of policies verify pushdown predicate result superset/subset properties vs full auth evaluation. Also fuzz IAM join cases.

sam: Alerting: page if mismatch_rate > 0.05% over 15m OR p99 latency increases > 20% after enabling for tenant. Metric names: console.pushdown.mismatch_rate, console.pushdown.p99_latency.

infra-bot: integration tests: added policy-compiler unit tests. ci-bot: pipeline green for branch `feature/policy-pushdown`.

rachel: infra ops asks for a kill-switch. We should add tenant-level feature-flag to turn off pushdown and fallback immediately to proxy masking. Also an emergency global toggle.

maria: agreed. Final question: where to author policies? central IAM UI or console? Prefer central IAM but console needs lightweight overrides. We'll coordinate with product.

oliver: next up I'll PR the policy-compiler prototype + plan cache integration. Sam and Rachel want to review the security corner cases.

sam: i'll take ownership of the sampling harness and mismatch diff job.

maria: thanks — i'll produce the rollout checklist and update RFC with the hybrid fallback approach. Ping me if you want to pair on auth_version scheme. :wave:
